text:
alina: FYI pushed a short follow-up to the gateway hedging RFC. Trying to capture the rollback semantics when we do an in-flight hedge + partial stream reassembly. https://go/repo/hedge-rfc

tariq: skimmed. main question: if we hedge to a fallback model midstream and the fallback returns a short partial token plus trailers, how do we avoid double-applying side-effects?

drew: short answer: we need an idempotency surface plus a pre-commit hook. longer: we can emit an "hedge-id" header and require upstreams to accept a commit token before applying side-effects. if committoken never arrives, no side-effect.

maria: that matches what we do for DurableWrites in Dedicated, but two gaps: 1) streaming responses need a way to send a provisional progress token, and 2) spine/sidecar protocol must be light-weight for latency-sensitive requests.

alina: agreed. proposal in doc: 1) add X-Rw-Hedge-Id on hedged requests 2) upstream returns X-Rw-Prog: <offset> in trailers 3) final commit uses /commit?hedge=<id> with basic auth. If commit fails we fallback to idempotent compensating action.

tariq: what about client retries? if client retries with a new request we might get a new hedge-id and duplicate commits. Need global dedupe key (user-generated idempotency-key) + hedge-id.

drew: yeah we should prefer client-provided idempotency-key. Server only uses hedge-id for in-flight correlation. Dedupempotency lookup order: idempotency-key -> commit-status. cheap in Redis.

maria: edge case: streaming partial responses mean we might have already emitted tokens to client before commit. Apps expect optimistic progress. If commit fails we need a graceful downgrade path: send trailer "x-rw-finality: uncertain" and recommend client switch to read-only fallback.

alina: tradeoff: extra roundtrip for commit increases tail latency for successful hedges. But without it we risk invisible side-effects. We could make commit async for non-critical side-effects and provide a webhook/event for finality. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

drew: async commit for non-blocking ops sounds good. But we need observability: per-hedge metrics (hedge-latency, commit-latency, commit-failures) and a small SLA/contract for apps.

tariq: operational question: can the gateway proxy hold onto KV-cache windows keyed by hedge-id to let fallback resume midstream without reparsing full context? memory pressure concerns.

maria: we can TTL those windows aggressively (1-2s) and backpressure hedging when memory > threshold. Also expose a feature flag per-tenant to disable in-flight KV snapshotting.

alina: pseudo-config in doc:
```
edge.hedge:
  enabled: true
  window_ttl_ms: 1500
  max_cached_windows: 10000
  idempotency_lookup: redis://dedupe
  async_commit_nonblocking: true
```

infra-bot: deploy:arch-proposals has applied changes to the docs branch (hedge-rfc/v2) by alina at 2024-11-22T09:14:00Z :white_check_mark:


drew: next steps: I can prototype the hedge-id header and trailer flow in proxy v2 (small change). Maria can sketch the operational toggle. Tariq will draft the client docs (recommended header usage). Alina will update RFC with commit vs async decision by EOD.

alina: thanks all — will update. If anyone wants to discuss live, ping me and I'll set a 30-min deep-dive. :calendar:
